idiom_name: Array<T>.reduce<U>(callback, initialValue) / reduceRight with a declared accumulator type
implementation_notes: TypeScript types JavaScript's array fold directly: reduce<U>(callback: (previousValue: U, currentValue: T, index: number, array: T[]) => U, initialValue: U): U lets the accumulator's type be declared independently of the element type - which is exactly the algebra's carrier - and passing initialValue is what makes the carrier inferable (without it the overload returns T and an empty array throws at run time). For a structural fold over a discriminated union the idiom is a recursive function with a switch on the discriminant, where TypeScript's control-flow analysis narrows each arm and a `never` assignment in the default arm converts a forgotten case into a compile error. There is no runtime fold over readonly arrays (Array.prototype methods do not exist on ReadonlyArray), so a readonly pipeline is copied or folded through an iterator instead.
pitfalls: Omitting the initial value changes the overload's return type to the element type and throws TypeError on an empty array: an explicitly typed accumulator plus an initial value is the only safe spelling for a general fold.

Leaving U to inference widens nothing: reduce((a, b) => a + b) infers the element type as the carrier, so building a string or an object from numeric elements concatenates or fails at the wrong place unless the type argument or the seed fixes the carrier.

ReadonlyArray<T> has no reduce (and no other mutating Array method), so a readonly pipeline must be copied/spread first or folded through an iterator, and the array fold is single-threaded and stack-bound - deep recursive folds need an explicit worklist.

variants.name: Lazy iterator pipeline folded with Iterator.reduce (typed by IteratorObject)
variants.implementation_notes: Once the target lib includes the ES2025 iterator helpers, TypeScript types the native iterator methods: version 5.6 introduced IteratorObject<T, TReturn, TNext> to describe built-in iterators (ArrayIterator, MapIterator, generator objects) that carry map/filter/take/flatMap/reduce, Iterator.from adapts any Iterable/Iterator into that type, and generators therefore gain a typed lazy pipeline without a helper library. A fold over such a chain is lazy until the final reduce - which is not lazy itself, since it drains the iterator - so intermediate arrays disappear but unbounded sources must be bounded in the chain. It throws TypeError for an empty iterator without an initialValue, exactly like the array method, and the type is single-use: a consumed iterator cannot be re-folded.
pitfalls: The chain is lazy but the fold is not: an unbounded generator must be bounded with take/takeWhile inside the chain, because reduce drains everything the pipeline yields.

IteratorObject typing requires the esnext lib (TypeScript 5.6+) and a 2025-era runtime (Node 22+): under an older lib the methods are type errors even where a polyfill would work at run time, so the lib and the runtime floor have to agree with the deployment target.

Iterators are single-use and helpers live on iterators rather than iterables: an array or Set needs .values() or Iterator.from(), and re-running a fold means rebuilding the chain (which is why a reusable generator function is the natural source).
